boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all seven frozen records in Jackson’s Valley Campaign. Preserve per-engagement dates, including Princeton’s May 15–17 interval and separate Cross Keys/Port Republic dates. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Frozen numeric side strengths are blank; formation names and incomplete losses cannot fill them.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads District of the Kanawha [US]; Army of East Kentucky and Col. Gabriel C. Wharton's Brigade, Department of Southwest Virginia [CS].
claims.rationale: Source field only. Formations, engaged troops and changing concentrations do not establish matched opening populations. Live zeros are not measured absence; shared provenance is not independent corroboration.

claims.rationale: The frozen summary locates the fighting in Mercer County around Princeton but does not establish battlefield ground or defensible positions. No battle-specific map or topographic passage was retained.
No battle-specific supply, ammunition or transport return was inspected. Formation lists and retrospective descriptions are not readiness measures.
No original reconnaissance, order or message chain was inspected to establish contemporary knowledge. Surprise in a summary does not independently establish what each commander knew.

claims.rationale: Operational context, not an inspected original order or a verified measure of the railroad’s capacity.

claims.value: The frozen narrative places Marshall against two of Cox’s brigades during May 15–17; Crook’s brigade is described separately at Lewisburg on May 23.
claims.rationale: Preserve the three-day Princeton interval. Crook’s later action is not automatically part of Princeton or equal commander credit.

claims.value: The Princeton narrative dates the later Winchester routing of Banks to March 25, whereas the frozen First Winchester record is dated May 25.
claims.rationale: Retain the literal conflict. The separate Winchester record supplies the explicit May date; this pass does not silently repair raw text or move that later action into Princeton’s result.

claims.value: The frozen result remains Confederate victory.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 129 total (US 23k/69w/21m; CS incomplete, Marshall 4k/12w, Wharton no report).
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. Confederate coverage is explicitly incomplete: Marshall supplies 4 killed and 12 wounded, Wharton has no report. The numerical 129 is a partial reported sum, not a complete battle loss or a known zero for Wharton.

open_questions: Original orders, returns, casualty reconciliation, contemporary message chains and precise command clocks remain deferred after the bounded pass. No whole-book, facsimile or map verification is claimed.

NPS/CWSAC is one family; Allan is one interested retrospective history where used. Embedded reports are not additional independently inspected families. Princeton retains only the frozen NPS/CWSAC family.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
